title: A shared first step for MAP2K1 and RAF1 families

sentences.text: From RASopathies Network, we invite Noonan Syndrome Association (UK) to explore collaboration for families affected by MAP2K1-related cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome.
MAP2K1 and RAF1 both take part in the MAPK pathway, a chain of signals within cells.
The atlas infers your support for RAF1 families from your wider Noonan syndrome remit; your website does not name RAF1.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: CFC International's CITIZEN CFC Syndrome Registry offers a starting point; its inclusion of MAP2K1 families is inferred by the atlas from its CFC coverage.
PATRAS and our developing contact registry are other resources, although their MAP2K1 coverage is also atlas-inferred.
We propose sharing registry information first, not promising access or transferring family records.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please help check whether RAF1 families experience heat intolerance, excessive sweating or wide mouth, rather than treating missing records as absence.
For broader comparisons, also check heat intolerance, keratosis pilaris and excessive sweating in RIT1 and Costello families.
The MAP2K1 “protein does too much” explanation is contested: the studied variants still require upstream signals; RAF1 variants can increase or impair protein activity.
Before borrowing the MEK162 study design, review eligibility and the listed symptom gaps—heat intolerance, excessive sweating and five unspecified others; its RAF1 link is atlas-inferred.
Check both questions below, keeping any treatment discussion limited to published evidence to discuss with a neurologist.
Let us send one joint enquiry to CFC International asking whether CITIZEN registry information could be offered to RAF1 families and what eligibility checks would be needed.
Is MEK inhibition used or tested in cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome involving BRAF, MAP2K1 or KRAS, or in HRAS-related Costello syndrome?
Which individual variants increase activity, impair the protein's working ability or cause loss of function?
Dear Noonan Syndrome Association (UK),
Could we explore a small registry-information collaboration?
MAP2K1 and RAF1 share the MAPK signalling pathway.
Could we jointly ask CFC International about sharing CITIZEN registry information with RAF1 families this month?
We would confirm eligibility before inviting participation.
Thank you for considering this first step.
[Your name], on behalf of RASopathies Network (RASopathiesNet USA / UK)
